transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Please do not attempt any internal electrical tests on a microwave; the capacitors store a lethal charge even when unplugged, and opening the casing exposes you to high voltage. To help narrow this down safely: were you using a standard 'Full Power' or 'Auto Cook' setting, or was it set to Defrost/Low Power? Also, did the microwave actually start cooking (did the timer count down)?
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
It was on full power, and yes the timer counts down as normal, just no heat. Water stays cold after a minute. It's unplugged now though, and I did get a loud buzz once just before it stopped heating.

That loud buzz is a very useful clue: it suggests a fault in the high-voltage circuit, most commonly a shorted high-voltage diode or a failing magnetron. To help me confirm exactly which part is likely at fault (and to check if your model might be under warranty), could you please read the model number from the rating plate? It is usually on the back of the microwave or inside the door frame.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Samsung MS23K3513AW/EU, about 4 years old. Cost about £100 new.

Since the unit is about 4 years old and cost around £100, it may still be covered by Samsung’s standard one-year warranty (with proof of purchase) or potentially longer depending on your specific terms. Because these components carry a lethal charge even when unplugged, you must not attempt to test or replace them yourself; please contact Samsung support to check your warranty status and arrange for an engineer to visit.
